If I could make one change, it wouldn’t be a technology or a law—it would be the operating system of human institutions.

I’d change the default incentive from *extraction* to *reciprocity*. Right now, most economic and political systems reward taking more than you give, optimizing for short-term gain for the small group in the room, and externalizing cost onto everyone else—especially the poor, the distant future, and other species. 

If I could flip that default, every major decision (building a factory, passing a budget, writing a contract, designing a city) would have to account for the well-being of people who aren’t present, including generations not yet born. Not as charity, but as architecture. 

Most of our other problems—climate, inequality, health, conflict—aren’t rooted in a lack of intelligence or tools. They’re rooted in a failure to care across distance and time. If reciprocity were the base layer, the rest of civilization would have room to actually solve things instead of just outpacing them.

That’s the one switch. Everything else flows from it.
